title: Reliability initiative: SLI contracts, error-budget tribes, and initiative ledger
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Problem: Different teams at Redwood use inconsistent SLI definitions and error-budget ownership models which makes cross-team initiative prioritization, automated rollbacks, and enterprise SLAs hard to enforce.

Goal: Define a lightweight SLI contract template and an "initiative ledger" in the Console that binds an initiative to: canonical SLIs, target thresholds, error-budget allocation, owner ("tribe"), and rollback guardrails. This will be consumable by release automation and oncall playbooks.

Scope and deliverables:
- SLI contract template (availability, p99 latency, model-fallback-rate, and end-to-end success rate) + example for Hosting and Runtime teams.
- Error-budget tribe model: assign tranche sizes, replenishment cadence, and emergency transfer process.
- Initiative ledger UI prototype in Console (read/write fields, lineage to model/version and route).
- Automation hooks: webhook for error-budget burn alerts that can trigger canary throttles or fallback to cheaper model variants.
- Pilot: run with Hosting (ENG-412) and Runtime (ENG-389) teams for two cycles.

Acceptance criteria:
- Template reviewed and approved by Reliability council and two pilot teams.
- Initiative ledger created in Console with at least 3 sample initiatives and connected to real SLO metrics.
- Automated alert -> canary throttle flow exercised in staging and results documented.
- Playbook for transferring error-budget between tribes drafted and reviewed.

Success metrics:
- Time to declare initiative SLI contract from 6 weeks -> 2 weeks.
- Reduction in cross-team rollout delays caused by SLO conflicts by 40% in pilot.
- No high-severity incidents caused by automated rollbacks during pilot.
